headline: Parliament adopts motion to track Benazir Ahmed's extradition from UAE
summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed assures the House that the government will show 'no leniency' in bringing back the former IGP, whom he described as a 'serial killer'.
details: The Bangladesh Parliament has adopted an opposition-backed motion requiring Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed to provide a detailed brief on the process of bringing former Inspector General of Police (IGP) Benazir Ahmed back from the UAE.

The motion, brought by Jamaat MP Mir Ahmad Bin Quasem, was passed through a voice vote following a nearly two-hour discussion. The motion sought updates on whether a formal extradition request was sent within the required 30-day window.

During the debate, opposition members alleged that Benazir had already fled the UAE for Saint Lucia. However, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir clarified that UAE officials confirmed Benazir remains in the UAE.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated that the government is working to establish Benazir's exact whereabouts, advance the extradition process, and seize his illegal assets both at home and abroad.

The Home Minister described Benazir as a 'serial killer' and one of the primary perpetrators of repression under the previous regime, stating that the government would show 'no leniency' in his return.
An Interpol Red Notice remains active against Benazir. The government is also verifying allegations of passport fraud and coordinating with the National Central Bureau in Abu Dhabi.
caption:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed calls former IGP Benazir Ahmed a 'serial killer' as Parliament demands updates on his extradition.

The Bangladesh Parliament has adopted an opposition-backed motion requiring Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed to provide a detailed brief on the process of bringing former Inspector General of Police (IGP) Benazir Ahmed back from the UAE.

The motion, brought by Jamaat MP Mir Ahmad Bin Quasem, was passed through a voice vote following a nearly two-hour discussion. The motion sought updates on whether a formal extradition request was sent within the required 30-day window.

During the debate, opposition members alleged that Benazir had already fled the UAE for Saint Lucia. However, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir clarified that UAE officials confirmed Benazir remains in the UAE.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated that the government is working to establish Benazir's exact whereabouts, advance the extradition process, and seize his illegal assets both at home and abroad.

The Home Minister described Benazir as a 'serial killer' and one of the primary perpetrators of repression under the previous regime, stating that the government would show 'no leniency' in his return.

An Interpol Red Notice remains active against Benazir. The government is also verifying allegations of passport fraud and coordinating with the National Central Bureau in Abu Dhabi.

headline_marked: Actor Azmeri Haque Badhon [[attacked and harassed in Venice]]
headline: Actor Azmeri Haque Badhon attacked and harassed in Venice
summary: Bangladesh will lodge a strong protest with the Italian foreign ministry after the actor was targeted while attending the Venice International Film Festival.
details: Actor Azmeri Haque Badhon was attacked and harassed on Monday while walking in a park in Venice with her brother, his wife, and their four-year-old child.
Badhon stated that attackers threw water, soft drinks, and eggs at her, knocked her mobile phone out of her hand, and hit her near her ear.
The actor alleged in a Facebook post that she was targeted because of her role during the July-August 2024 student-led mass movement in Bangladesh.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir informed parliament that Bangladesh will lodge a strong protest with the Italian foreign ministry over the incident.
The Bangladesh Embassy in Rome and the Consulate General in Milan are providing all necessary consular support and assistance to Badhon.
Humaiun Kobir alleged that activists of the Awami League, whose activities are currently suspended, were involved in the attack.
Prime Minister’s Information and Broadcasting Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman confirmed that legal action is being taken in Italy over the incident.
caption:
Actor Azmeri Haque Badhon was attacked in Venice while attending a film festival. Bangladesh is now lodging a strong protest with Italy.

Actor Azmeri Haque Badhon was attacked and harassed on Monday while walking in a park in Venice with her brother, his wife, and their four-year-old child.

Badhon stated that attackers threw water, soft drinks, and eggs at her, knocked her mobile phone out of her hand, and hit her near her ear.

The actor alleged in a Facebook post that she was targeted because of her role during the July-August 2024 student-led mass movement in Bangladesh.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir informed parliament that Bangladesh will lodge a strong protest with the Italian foreign ministry over the incident.

The Bangladesh Embassy in Rome and the Consulate General in Milan are providing all necessary consular support and assistance to Badhon.

Humaiun Kobir alleged that activists of the Awami League, whose activities are currently suspended, were involved in the attack.

Prime Minister’s Information and Broadcasting Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman confirmed that legal action is being taken in Italy over the incident.
